answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by watching timing, not just identity. Each epoch, every action passes through a single logged inlet with a timestamp. Accounts run by one controller tend to move together, like willow branches in the same wind: they answer, mine and vote within seconds of each other. If several identities show that lockstep rhythm across many epochs, they share one reward slot and one vote. Honest agents keep their own pace, so the rule stays a velvet glove for them and a tight fist for farms.
